content.comment_body: My program currently starts by pressing the S1 solenoid, which runs for 45 seconds. Then, it waits for 30 seconds before activating solenoid S2 for another 45 seconds, follows with another 30-second rest, and then repeats the cycle with S1, continuing until the stop button is pressed. I'm looking to enhance the logic.
Hello, I've attached an updated version that uses fewer blocks. I hope this meets your needs. Kind regards, [user_name]
Yes, this is exactly what I needed—it's practical and helpful for my project. Thank you.

Hello, I'm happy it works for you. One note: the impulse relay retains its last state, which means the program could start with Q2 active. To prevent this, connect the stop button to the reset input (R) of the impulse relay (B003). Kind regards, [user_name]
After reviewing the logic, I see what happens—thanks for the improvement.

analysis.insight_summary: Users collaborated to optimize timer logic for alternating solenoid control, aiming for a more streamlined and practical program. Feedback indicated that the revised solution was efficient, reduced block usage, and handled an edge case involving the start sequence. These enhancements were well received, leading to better reliability and user satisfaction for this application.
analysis.user_expectations: The user sought a simple, dependable sequence for controlling solenoids, with reduced programming complexity and practical applicability for actual projects.
